title: Apple Poised to Unveil Major MacBook Air Redesign in 2025, Reports Gurman
body:
Apple is reportedly gearing up for a two‑phase refresh of its flagship ultra‑light laptop, with a new MacBook Air powered by the upcoming M6 silicon slated for release early next year and a more radical redesign potentially arriving as early as 2027. The speculation comes from veteran Apple analyst Mark Gurman, who hinted on his recent podcast that the company may be planning a “big MacBook Air overhaul” that could reshape the product’s design, performance envelope, and feature set within the next few years.

The first wave of the update is expected to be a fairly incremental upgrade. Apple’s current Air, introduced in 2022 with the M2 chip, has been praised for its thin profile, fan‑less architecture, and solid battery life, but it has also faced criticism for a modest performance ceiling and a design that has seen little change since its debut. The anticipated M6‑based model is likely to retain the familiar wedge‑shaped chassis while offering a noticeable boost in CPU and GPU cores, higher‑bandwidth memory, and possibly an expanded battery capacity to keep pace with the more demanding workloads that the newer silicon can handle. Early rumours also suggest a brighter, higher‑refresh‑rate display and incremental improvements to the webcam and speaker system, aligning the Air more closely with the capabilities of Apple’s higher‑end MacBook Pro line.

What sets Gurman’s latest forecast apart is the suggestion that Apple is already sketching a far more ambitious redesign for the Air, one that could debut in 2027. While Apple has not confirmed any such plans, the analyst’s track record of accurate leaks lends weight to the possibility. A “big overhaul” could involve a shift to a completely flat, edge‑to‑edge glass panel, a slimmer footprint achieved through advances in silicon packaging, and the integration of next‑generation ports such as a USB‑C/Thunderbolt 5 hybrid that supports even faster data transfer and charging rates. There is also speculation that Apple may finally bring the Air into the fold of its proprietary “ProMotion” technology, offering variable refresh rates up to 120 Hz, which would dramatically improve the visual experience for both creative work and media consumption.

Industry observers see this potential timeline as part of Apple’s broader strategy to keep the Air relevant in a market increasingly crowded with thin‑and‑light laptops from competitors like Dell, Lenovo, and Microsoft. By staggering upgrades—first a modest performance bump with the M6, then a more transformative redesign—Apple can maintain a steady revenue stream from the Air’s sizable user base while buying time to refine the technologies that will underpin a next‑generation device. The 2027 overhaul could also coincide with the maturation of Apple’s silicon roadmap, perhaps featuring the M8 or even a new “Apple Silicon” architecture that leverages advanced 3‑nanometer processes and integrated AI accelerators.

Analysts also note that the timing may be influenced by supply‑chain considerations and the company’s broader product cadence. Apple typically staggers major hardware refreshes to avoid cannibalizing sales of its higher‑margin MacBook Pro models, and a later, more dramatic Air redesign could serve as a bridge between the current generation and the next wave of Mac hardware that may incorporate features like foldable displays or ultra‑thin form factors. Moreover, a 2027 launch would give Apple ample runway to address lingering consumer concerns about repairability and sustainability, areas where the company has faced criticism in recent years.

If Gurman’s predictions hold true, the next few years could see the MacBook Air evolving from a reliable, entry‑level workhorse into a flagship‑class device that blurs the line between thin‑and‑light and professional laptops. Consumers and professionals alike will be watching closely for official announcements, especially as Apple’s silicon roadmap continues to push the envelope of performance and efficiency. The forthcoming M6‑powered Air will set the stage, but the true test will be whether Apple can deliver a 2027 redesign that not only refreshes the aesthetic but also introduces substantive innovations that keep the Air at the forefront of the portable computing market.
